On top of that, my physical body literally feels heavy and exhausted all the time, making even basic tasks feel impossible.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any loss of interest in activities that you used to enjoy before your knee procedure, or has your lack of participation been solely due to your physical limitations?\n\nPatient: It’s definitely more than just my physical limitations; I’ve lost all interest in the things that used to light me up. I feel this blank indifference toward my financial workshops, senior hikes, and even my gardening, so I just sit in front of the TV instead of joining in. I look at my tools and flyers and feel absolutely nothing.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific situation or thought that triggers your feelings of guilt about letting others down, and how you typically respond to those feelings?\n\nPatient: It hits me hardest when I think about missing book club or how I can't drive my friends to the bank anymore, which makes me feel like \"dead weight\" who is failing everyone. When those thoughts spiral, I usually just turn on the TV and ignore phone calls from my friends and mentees. Facing them feels far too overwhelming when I feel so useless.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever experience any pleasure or enjoy any activities at all, even small ones like reading, talking to a friend, or taking a warm bath, or has the pleasure been completely absent from your life since you started feeling this way?\n\nPatient: No, the pleasure has been completely absent lately. I feel this blank indifference toward everything that used to light me up, like my hiking or my gardening. I have to remind myself to eat because nothing appeals to me, and by mid-afternoon, I've usually only picked at a piece of toast or some yogurt. At night, I lie awake for hours worrying about my knee, wake up multiple times, and then pop awake around 4 or 5 a.m. exhausted and unable to drift back off.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you weren't alive since you started feeling this way?\n\nPatient: Sometimes, on the really low days, I do catch myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up in the morning, or how quiet everything would be for everyone if I just slipped away. It just hasn't let up since then.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods, even brief, where your mood slightly improved or you felt slightly better, or has it been a constant, unrelenting feeling of sadness and worthlessness for the entire month?\n\nPatient: No, there haven't been any breaks or times when my mood improved at all. It has just been a constant, unrelenting heavy cloud hanging over me every single day since I realized I wasn't bouncing back from my knee procedure.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your feelings of sadness, worthlessness, and loss of interest in activities have impacted your daily functioning and relationships with others over the past month?\n\nPatient: Over the past month, my life has completely stalled. On top of that, my physical body literally feels heavy and exhausted all the time, making even basic tasks feel impossible.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any loss of interest in activities that you used to enjoy before your knee procedure, or has your lack of participation been solely due to your physical limitations?\n\nPatient: It’s definitely more than just my physical limitations; I’ve lost all interest in the things that used to light me up. I feel this blank indifference toward my financial workshops, senior hikes, and even my gardening, so I just sit in front of the TV instead of joining in. I look at my tools and flyers and feel absolutely nothing.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific situation or thought that triggers your feelings of guilt about letting others down, and how you typically respond to those feelings?\n\nPatient: It hits me hardest when I think about missing book club or how I can't drive my friends to the bank anymore, which makes me feel like \"dead weight\" who is failing everyone. When those thoughts spiral, I usually just turn on the TV and ignore phone calls from my friends and mentees. Facing them feels far too overwhelming when I feel so useless.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever experience any pleasure or enjoy any activities at all, even small ones like reading, talking to a friend, or taking a warm bath, or has the pleasure been completely absent from your life since you started feeling this way?\n\nPatient: No, the pleasure has been completely absent lately. I feel this blank indifference toward everything that used to light me up, like my hiking or my gardening. Instead of answering calls or trying to do anything, I just turn on the TV and sit there feeling absolutely nothing.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since you started feeling this way, such as eating more or less than usual, or sleeping more or less than usual?\n\nPatient: Yes, both have changed completely. I have to remind myself to eat because nothing appeals to me, and by mid-afternoon, I've usually only picked at a piece of toast or some yogurt. At night, I lie awake for hours worrying about my knee, wake up multiple times, and then pop awake around 4 or 5 a.m. exhausted and unable to drift back off.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you weren't alive since you started feeling this way?\n\nPatient: Sometimes, on the really low days, I do catch myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up in the morning, or how quiet everything would be for everyone if I just slipped away. But I haven't made any concrete plans to actually do anything to harm myself, if that makes sense. It's just a heavy, weary feeling that comes over me when I'm exhausted.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling indifferent to activities you used to enjoy, but can you think of anything, no matter how small, that you still find some pleasure in or look forward to, even if it's just slightly?\n\nPatient: Honestly, there really isn't anything right now that brings me pleasure or that I look forward to. Even when I turn on the TV, it's not because I enjoy it; I'm just sitting there staring at the screen to pass the time in a state of blank indifference.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned having thoughts about not wanting to wake up or slipping away, but not making any plans to harm yourself. Have these thoughts been recurring, or were they just a one-time thing, and do you feel like you're at risk of acting on them?\n\nPatient: Yes, they do recur, especially on those really low days when the exhaustion and guilt feel particularly heavy. But I want to reassure you that they are just passive thoughts of wishing to slip away; I don't have any plans to harm myself, and I don't feel at risk of acting on them.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if your feelings of sadness, emptiness, and worthlessness, as well as your loss of interest in activities, have been present every day since they started, or have they varied in intensity over the past month?\n\nPatient: Yes, they have been present pretty steadily and consistently every single day for about the past month, rather than coming and going. This constant heavy feeling really took hold a couple of weeks after my knee procedure, once I realized I wasn't recovering as quickly as I had hoped. It just hasn't let up since then.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods, even brief, where your mood slightly improved or you felt slightly better, or has it been a constant, unrelenting feeling of sadness and worthlessness for the entire month?\n\nPatient: No, there haven't been any breaks or times when my mood improved at all. It has just been a constant, unrelenting heavy cloud hanging over me every single day since I realized I wasn't bouncing back from my knee procedure.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your feelings of sadness, worthlessness, and loss of interest in activities have impacted your daily functioning and relationships with others over the past month?\n\nPatient: Over the past month, my life has completely stalled. I've gone from running workshops and social events to canceling almost everything, barely keeping up with basic chores, and actively avoiding calls from my friends and mentees. It all just feels too overwhelming to handle when I feel like such dead weight.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned a complete loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy, but can you think of any small moments or instances where you felt even a slight spark of interest or pleasure in something, even if it was fleeting?\n\nPatient: No, I really haven't felt even a fleeting spark of interest or pleasure lately. When I look at my gardening tools or the flyers for my workshops, I just feel a blank indifference. I end up just sitting in front of the TV because absolutely nothing sparks any interest in me anymore.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced episodes of depression like this before, or is this the first time you've felt this way, and if so, how have they affected your life in the past?\n\nPatient: No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before in my life. This is the very first time I've ever felt this way, which is why it has been so unsettling for me.\n\nDoctor: Since this is your first episode of feeling this way, can you tell me if you think the duration of your current feelings of sadness and worthlessness, which have been constant for about a month, might be related to the fact that you've never had a depressive episode before, or if you think it's more closely tied to your recent knee procedure and the subsequent change in your lifestyle?"

I had an unexpected knee procedure a few weeks ago that completely sidelined me, and I've had to pull back from all my community volunteering and activities. It’s just been really hard feeling like I'm no longer the active person everyone was relying on.\n\nDoctor: Did you start feeling useless and letting everyone down immediately after your knee procedure, or did these feelings develop over time as you were recovering?\n\nPatient: It didn't start right away, but about two weeks after the procedure when I realized I wasn't bouncing back like I'd hoped. Once it became clear how slow my recovery would be, this heavy feeling set in, and it's been hanging over me steadily for about a month now.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'this heavy feeling' - is it more about feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, or is it more about feeling anxious, worried, or on edge about your situation?\n\nPatient: Honestly, it’s a mix of both. I feel a deep, empty sadness like I’m just dead weight and completely useless to everyone now, combined with constant, looping worries about my knee and how I'm letting people down. On top of that, my physical body literally feels heavy and exhausted all the time, making even basic tasks feel impossible.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any loss of interest in activities that you used to enjoy before your knee procedure, or has your lack of participation been solely due to your physical limitations?\n\nPatient: It’s definitely more than just my physical limitations; I’ve lost all interest in the things that used to light me up. I feel this blank indifference toward my financial workshops, senior hikes, and even my gardening, so I just sit in front of the TV instead of joining in. I look at my tools and flyers and feel absolutely nothing.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific situation or thought that triggers your feelings of guilt about letting others down, and how you typically respond to those feelings?\n\nPatient: It hits me hardest when I think about missing book club or how I can't drive my friends to the bank anymore, which makes me feel like \"dead weight\" who is failing everyone. When those thoughts spiral, I usually just turn on the TV and ignore phone calls from my friends and mentees. Facing them feels far too overwhelming when I feel so useless.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever experience any pleasure or enjoy any activities at all, even small ones like reading, talking to a friend, or taking a warm bath, or has the pleasure been completely absent from your life since you started feeling this way?\n\nPatient: No, the pleasure has been completely absent lately. I feel this blank indifference toward everything that used to light me up, like my hiking or my gardening. Instead of answering calls or trying to do anything, I just turn on the TV and sit there feeling absolutely nothing.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since you started feeling this way, such as eating more or less than usual, or sleeping more or less than usual?\n\nPatient: Yes, both have changed completely. I have to remind myself to eat because nothing appeals to me, and by mid-afternoon, I've usually only picked at a piece of toast or some yogurt. At night, I lie awake for hours worrying about my knee, wake up multiple times, and then pop awake around 4 or 5 a.m. exhausted and unable to drift back off.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you weren't alive since you started feeling this way?\n\nPatient: Sometimes, on the really low days, I do catch myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up in the morning, or how quiet everything would be for everyone if I just slipped away. But I haven't made any concrete plans to actually do anything to harm myself, if that makes sense. It's just a heavy, weary feeling that comes over me when I'm exhausted.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling indifferent to activities you used to enjoy, but can you think of anything, no matter how small, that you still find some pleasure in or look forward to, even if it's just slightly?\n\nPatient: Honestly, there really isn't anything right now that brings me pleasure or that I look forward to. Even when I turn on the TV, it's not because I enjoy it; I'm just sitting there staring at the screen to pass the time in a state of blank indifference.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned having thoughts about not wanting to wake up or slipping away, but not making any plans to harm yourself. Have these thoughts been recurring, or were they just a one-time thing, and do you feel like you're at risk of acting on them?\n\nPatient: Yes, they do recur, especially on those really low days when the exhaustion and guilt feel particularly heavy. But I want to reassure you that they are just passive thoughts of wishing to slip away; I don't have any plans to harm myself, and I don't feel at risk of acting on them.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if your feelings of sadness, emptiness, and worthlessness, as well as your loss of interest in activities, have been present every day since they started, or have they varied in intensity over the past month?\n\nPatient: Yes, they have been present pretty steadily and consistently every single day for about the past month, rather than coming and going. This constant heavy feeling really took hold a couple of weeks after my knee procedure, once I realized I wasn't recovering as quickly as I had hoped. It just hasn't let up since then.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods, even brief, where your mood slightly improved or you felt slightly better, or has it been a constant, unrelenting feeling of sadness and worthlessness for the entire month?\n\nPatient: No, there haven't been any breaks or times when my mood improved at all. It has just been a constant, unrelenting heavy cloud hanging over me every single day since I realized I wasn't bouncing back from my knee procedure.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your feelings of sadness, worthlessness, and loss of interest in activities have impacted your daily functioning and relationships with others over the past month?\n\nPatient: Over the past month, my life has completely stalled. I've gone from running workshops and social events to canceling almost everything, barely keeping up with basic chores, and actively avoiding calls from my friends and mentees. It all just feels too overwhelming to handle when I feel like such dead weight.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned a complete loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy, but can you think of any small moments or instances where you felt even a slight spark of interest or pleasure in something, even if it was fleeting?\n\nPatient: No, I really haven't felt even a fleeting spark of interest or pleasure lately. When I look at my gardening tools or the flyers for my workshops, I just feel a blank indifference. I end up just sitting in front of the TV because absolutely nothing sparks any interest in me anymore.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced episodes of depression like this before, or is this the first time you've felt this way, and if so, how have they affected your life in the past?\n\nPatient: No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before in my life. This is the very first time I've ever felt this way, which is why it has been so unsettling for me.\n\nDoctor: Since this is your first episode of feeling this way, can you tell me if you think the duration of your current feelings of sadness and worthlessness, which have been constant for about a month, might be related to the fact that you've never had a depressive episode before, or if you think it's more closely tied to your recent knee procedure and the subsequent change in your lifestyle?\n\nPatient: I believe these feelings are directly tied to my knee procedure and the sudden, drastic change in my lifestyle. Before the fall, I was highly active, independent, and always helping others, so realizing I couldn't bounce back quickly is what triggered this spiral of feeling useless. It's definitely that sudden loss of my independence and feeling like a burden that has kept me in this state, rather than anything else.\n\nDoctor: You've had these feelings for about a month now, directly tied to your knee procedure and loss of independence. Can you help me understand if you believe these feelings would significantly improve if your physical condition and independence were to return to what they were before the procedure?"

Once it became clear how slow my recovery would be, this heavy feeling set in, and it's been hanging over me steadily for about a month now.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'this heavy feeling' - is it more about feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, or is it more about feeling anxious, worried, or on edge about your situation?\n\nPatient: Honestly, it’s a mix of both. It's just a heavy, weary feeling that comes over me when I'm exhausted.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling indifferent to activities you used to enjoy, but can you think of anything, no matter how small, that you still find some pleasure in or look forward to, even if it's just slightly?\n\nPatient: Honestly, there really isn't anything right now that brings me pleasure or that I look forward to. Even when I turn on the TV, it's not because I enjoy it; I'm just sitting there staring at the screen to pass the time in a state of blank indifference.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned having thoughts about not wanting to wake up or slipping away, but not making any plans to harm yourself. Have these thoughts been recurring, or were they just a one-time thing, and do you feel like you're at risk of acting on them?\n\nPatient: Yes, they do recur, especially on those really low days when the exhaustion and guilt feel particularly heavy. Before the fall, I was highly active, independent, and always helping others, so realizing I couldn't bounce back quickly is what triggered this spiral of feeling useless. Even if my knee physically heals, I feel so deeply useless, empty, and disconnected right now that I just can't imagine snapping back to my old self. I really worry that I've permanently let everyone down and that this empty feeling is here to stay.\n\nDoctor: Since you've never experienced an episode like this before and it's been about a month, do you think the fact that it's your first episode and has been persistent might suggest that it could be a single, severe episode of depression, or do you believe it might be the start of a recurring pattern of depressive episodes?\n\nPatient: I’m really not sure, as I’ve never gone through anything like this before in my life. I don't know if this is just a one-time thing or the start of some kind of pattern. Honestly, I'm just feeling so overwhelmed by how I feel right now that it's hard to even think about what comes next.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if you were able to return to your normal activities and volunteering, your feelings of sadness, worthlessness, and loss of interest would improve significantly, or do you believe these feelings have become more ingrained and less likely to resolve on their own?"

When those thoughts spiral, I usually just turn on the TV and ignore phone calls from my friends and mentees. Facing them feels far too overwhelming when I feel so useless.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever experience any pleasure or enjoy any activities at all, even small ones like reading, talking to a friend, or taking a warm bath, or has the pleasure been completely absent from your life since you started feeling this way?\n\nPatient: No, the pleasure has been completely absent lately. I feel this blank indifference toward everything that used to light me up, like my hiking or my gardening. Instead of answering calls or trying to do anything, I just turn on the TV and sit there feeling absolutely nothing.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since you started feeling this way, such as eating more or less than usual, or sleeping more or less than usual?\n\nPatient: Yes, both have changed completely. I have to remind myself to eat because nothing appeals to me, and by mid-afternoon, I've usually only picked at a piece of toast or some yogurt. At night, I lie awake for hours worrying about my knee, wake up multiple times, and then pop awake around 4 or 5 a.m. exhausted and unable to drift back off.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you weren't alive since you started feeling this way?\n\nPatient: Sometimes, on the really low days, I do catch myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up in the morning, or how quiet everything would be for everyone if I just slipped away. But I haven't made any concrete plans to actually do anything to harm myself, if that makes sense. It's just a heavy, weary feeling that comes over me when I'm exhausted.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling indifferent to activities you used to enjoy, but can you think of anything, no matter how small, that you still find some pleasure in or look forward to, even if it's just slightly?\n\nPatient: Honestly, there really isn't anything right now that brings me pleasure or that I look forward to. Even when I turn on the TV, it's not because I enjoy it; I'm just sitting there staring at the screen to pass the time in a state of blank indifference.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned having thoughts about not wanting to wake up or slipping away, but not making any plans to harm yourself. Have these thoughts been recurring, or were they just a one-time thing, and do you feel like you're at risk of acting on them?\n\nPatient: Yes, they do recur, especially on those really low days when the exhaustion and guilt feel particularly heavy. But I want to reassure you that they are just passive thoughts of wishing to slip away; I don't have any plans to harm myself, and I don't feel at risk of acting on them.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if your feelings of sadness, emptiness, and worthlessness, as well as your loss of interest in activities, have been present every day since they started, or have they varied in intensity over the past month?\n\nPatient: Yes, they have been present pretty steadily and consistently every single day for about the past month, rather than coming and going. This constant heavy feeling really took hold a couple of weeks after my knee procedure, once I realized I wasn't recovering as quickly as I had hoped. It just hasn't let up since then.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods, even brief, where your mood slightly improved or you felt slightly better, or has it been a constant, unrelenting feeling of sadness and worthlessness for the entire month?\n\nPatient: No, there haven't been any breaks or times when my mood improved at all. It has just been a constant, unrelenting heavy cloud hanging over me every single day since I realized I wasn't bouncing back from my knee procedure.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your feelings of sadness, worthlessness, and loss of interest in activities have impacted your daily functioning and relationships with others over the past month?\n\nPatient: Over the past month, my life has completely stalled. I've gone from running workshops and social events to canceling almost everything, barely keeping up with basic chores, and actively avoiding calls from my friends and mentees. It all just feels too overwhelming to handle when I feel like such dead weight.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned a complete loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy, but can you think of any small moments or instances where you felt even a slight spark of interest or pleasure in something, even if it was fleeting?\n\nPatient: No, I really haven't felt even a fleeting spark of interest or pleasure lately. When I look at my gardening tools or the flyers for my workshops, I just feel a blank indifference. I end up just sitting in front of the TV because absolutely nothing sparks any interest in me anymore.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced episodes of depression like this before, or is this the first time you've felt this way, and if so, how have they affected your life in the past?\n\nPatient: No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before in my life. This is the very first time I've ever felt this way, which is why it has been so unsettling for me.\n\nDoctor: Since this is your first episode of feeling this way, can you tell me if you think the duration of your current feelings of sadness and worthlessness, which have been constant for about a month, might be related to the fact that you've never had a depressive episode before, or if you think it's more closely tied to your recent knee procedure and the subsequent change in your lifestyle?\n\nPatient: I believe these feelings are directly tied to my knee procedure and the sudden, drastic change in my lifestyle. Before the fall, I was highly active, independent, and always helping others, so realizing I couldn't bounce back quickly is what triggered this spiral of feeling useless. It's definitely that sudden loss of my independence and feeling like a burden that has kept me in this state, rather than anything else.\n\nDoctor: You've had these feelings for about a month now, directly tied to your knee procedure and loss of independence. Can you help me understand if you believe these feelings would significantly improve if your physical condition and independence were to return to what they were before the procedure?\n\nPatient: I’d like to think that getting my mobility back would fix everything, since losing my independence is what triggered this downward spiral. But right now, I feel so hopeless, useless, and filled with blank indifference that it’s hard to even imagine returning to my old self. It's just really difficult to believe that things will ever get better.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your current feelings of sadness and worthlessness would likely resolve on their own once you've fully recovered from your knee procedure and regained your independence, or do you feel like these emotional struggles might persist even after your physical health improves?\n\nPatient: To be honest, I'm terrified that I might never return to my previous level of independence. Even if my knee physically heals, I feel so deeply useless, empty, and disconnected right now that I just can't imagine snapping back to my old self. I really worry that I've permanently let everyone down and that this empty feeling is here to stay.\n\nDoctor: Since you've never experienced an episode like this before and it's been about a month, do you think the fact that it's your first episode and has been persistent might suggest that it could be a single, severe episode of depression, or do you believe it might be the start of a recurring pattern of depressive episodes?\n\nPatient: I’m really not sure, as I’ve never gone through anything like this before in my life. I don't know if this is just a one-time thing or the start of some kind of pattern. Honestly, I'm just feeling so overwhelmed by how I feel right now that it's hard to even think about what comes next.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if you were able to return to your normal activities and volunteering, your feelings of sadness, worthlessness, and loss of interest would improve significantly, or do you believe these feelings have become more ingrained and less likely to resolve on their own?\n\nPatient: I'm afraid these feelings have become too deeply ingrained to just disappear, even if I were physically able to go back. When I look at my old volunteering flyers or gardening tools, I feel only a blank indifference, which makes me worry I'll never return to my previous level of independence. These thoughts of being useless and \"dead weight\" feel far too heavy to just go away.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your current emotional state is more likely a reaction to your recent life change and knee procedure, or could it be a sign of a more chronic condition that might recur in the future?\n\nPatient: I really feel this is a direct reaction to my knee procedure and the sudden loss of my active lifestyle. Before the fall, I was highly energetic, independent, and deeply involved in my community, and I have never experienced anything like this before. These feelings of uselessness only started once I realized I couldn't bounce back and participate in my usual activities.\n\nDoctor: Given that you've had these feelings for about a month and they seem closely tied to your knee procedure, do you think these feelings would likely recur if you faced another significant life change or health issue in the future, or do you believe this is a one-time response to your current situation?"

It’s just been really hard feeling like I'm no longer the active person everyone was relying on.\n\nDoctor: Did you start feeling useless and letting everyone down immediately after your knee procedure, or did these feelings develop over time as you were recovering?\n\nPatient: It didn't start right away, but about two weeks after the procedure when I realized I wasn't bouncing back like I'd hoped. Once it became clear how slow my recovery would be, this heavy feeling set in, and it's been hanging over me steadily for about a month now.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'this heavy feeling' - is it more about feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, or is it more about feeling anxious, worried, or on edge about your situation?\n\nPatient: Honestly, it’s a mix of both. I feel a deep, empty sadness like I’m just dead weight and completely useless to everyone now, combined with constant, looping worries about my knee and how I'm letting people down. On top of that, my physical body literally feels heavy and exhausted all the time, making even basic tasks feel impossible.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any loss of interest in activities that you used to enjoy before your knee procedure, or has your lack of participation been solely due to your physical limitations?\n\nPatient: It’s definitely more than just my physical limitations; I’ve lost all interest in the things that used to light me up. I feel this blank indifference toward my financial workshops, senior hikes, and even my gardening, so I just sit in front of the TV instead of joining in. I look at my tools and flyers and feel absolutely nothing.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific situation or thought that triggers your feelings of guilt about letting others down, and how you typically respond to those feelings?\n\nPatient: It hits me hardest when I think about missing book club or how I can't drive my friends to the bank anymore, which makes me feel like \"dead weight\" who is failing everyone. When those thoughts spiral, I usually just turn on the TV and ignore phone calls from my friends and mentees. Facing them feels far too overwhelming when I feel so useless.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever experience any pleasure or enjoy any activities at all, even small ones like reading, talking to a friend, or taking a warm bath, or has the pleasure been completely absent from your life since you started feeling this way?\n\nPatient: No, the pleasure has been completely absent lately. I feel this blank indifference toward everything that used to light me up, like my hiking or my gardening. Instead of answering calls or trying to do anything, I just turn on the TV and sit there feeling absolutely nothing.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since you started feeling this way, such as eating more or less than usual, or sleeping more or less than usual?\n\nPatient: Yes, both have changed completely. I have to remind myself to eat because nothing appeals to me, and by mid-afternoon, I've usually only picked at a piece of toast or some yogurt. At night, I lie awake for hours worrying about my knee, wake up multiple times, and then pop awake around 4 or 5 a.m. exhausted and unable to drift back off.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you weren't alive since you started feeling this way?\n\nPatient: Sometimes, on the really low days, I do catch myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up in the morning, or how quiet everything would be for everyone if I just slipped away. But I haven't made any concrete plans to actually do anything to harm myself, if that makes sense. It's just a heavy, weary feeling that comes over me when I'm exhausted.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling indifferent to activities you used to enjoy, but can you think of anything, no matter how small, that you still find some pleasure in or look forward to, even if it's just slightly?\n\nPatient: Honestly, there really isn't anything right now that brings me pleasure or that I look forward to. Even when I turn on the TV, it's not because I enjoy it; I'm just sitting there staring at the screen to pass the time in a state of blank indifference.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned having thoughts about not wanting to wake up or slipping away, but not making any plans to harm yourself. Have these thoughts been recurring, or were they just a one-time thing, and do you feel like you're at risk of acting on them?\n\nPatient: Yes, they do recur, especially on those really low days when the exhaustion and guilt feel particularly heavy. But I want to reassure you that they are just passive thoughts of wishing to slip away; I don't have any plans to harm myself, and I don't feel at risk of acting on them.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if your feelings of sadness, emptiness, and worthlessness, as well as your loss of interest in activities, have been present every day since they started, or have they varied in intensity over the past month?\n\nPatient: Yes, they have been present pretty steadily and consistently every single day for about the past month, rather than coming and going. This constant heavy feeling really took hold a couple of weeks after my knee procedure, once I realized I wasn't recovering as quickly as I had hoped. It just hasn't let up since then.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods, even brief, where your mood slightly improved or you felt slightly better, or has it been a constant, unrelenting feeling of sadness and worthlessness for the entire month?\n\nPatient: No, there haven't been any breaks or times when my mood improved at all. It has just been a constant, unrelenting heavy cloud hanging over me every single day since I realized I wasn't bouncing back from my knee procedure.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your feelings of sadness, worthlessness, and loss of interest in activities have impacted your daily functioning and relationships with others over the past month?\n\nPatient: Over the past month, my life has completely stalled. I've gone from running workshops and social events to canceling almost everything, barely keeping up with basic chores, and actively avoiding calls from my friends and mentees. It all just feels too overwhelming to handle when I feel like such dead weight.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned a complete loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy, but can you think of any small moments or instances where you felt even a slight spark of interest or pleasure in something, even if it was fleeting?\n\nPatient: No, I really haven't felt even a fleeting spark of interest or pleasure lately. When I look at my gardening tools or the flyers for my workshops, I just feel a blank indifference. I end up just sitting in front of the TV because absolutely nothing sparks any interest in me anymore.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced episodes of depression like this before, or is this the first time you've felt this way, and if so, how have they affected your life in the past?\n\nPatient: No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before in my life. This is the very first time I've ever felt this way, which is why it has been so unsettling for me.\n\nDoctor: Since this is your first episode of feeling this way, can you tell me if you think the duration of your current feelings of sadness and worthlessness, which have been constant for about a month, might be related to the fact that you've never had a depressive episode before, or if you think it's more closely tied to your recent knee procedure and the subsequent change in your lifestyle?\n\nPatient: I believe these feelings are directly tied to my knee procedure and the sudden, drastic change in my lifestyle. Before the fall, I was highly active, independent, and always helping others, so realizing I couldn't bounce back quickly is what triggered this spiral of feeling useless. It's definitely that sudden loss of my independence and feeling like a burden that has kept me in this state, rather than anything else.\n\nDoctor: You've had these feelings for about a month now, directly tied to your knee procedure and loss of independence. Can you help me understand if you believe these feelings would significantly improve if your physical condition and independence were to return to what they were before the procedure?\n\nPatient: I’d like to think that getting my mobility back would fix everything, since losing my independence is what triggered this downward spiral. But right now, I feel so hopeless, useless, and filled with blank indifference that it’s hard to even imagine returning to my old self. It's just really difficult to believe that things will ever get better.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your current feelings of sadness and worthlessness would likely resolve on their own once you've fully recovered from your knee procedure and regained your independence, or do you feel like these emotional struggles might persist even after your physical health improves?\n\nPatient: To be honest, I'm terrified that I might never return to my previous level of independence. Even if my knee physically heals, I feel so deeply useless, empty, and disconnected right now that I just can't imagine snapping back to my old self. I really worry that I've permanently let everyone down and that this empty feeling is here to stay.\n\nDoctor: Since you've never experienced an episode like this before and it's been about a month, do you think the fact that it's your first episode and has been persistent might suggest that it could be a single, severe episode of depression, or do you believe it might be the start of a recurring pattern of depressive episodes?\n\nPatient: I’m really not sure, as I’ve never gone through anything like this before in my life. I don't know if this is just a one-time thing or the start of some kind of pattern. Honestly, I'm just feeling so overwhelmed by how I feel right now that it's hard to even think about what comes next.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if you were able to return to your normal activities and volunteering, your feelings of sadness, worthlessness, and loss of interest would improve significantly, or do you believe these feelings have become more ingrained and less likely to resolve on their own?\n\nPatient: I'm afraid these feelings have become too deeply ingrained to just disappear, even if I were physically able to go back. When I look at my old volunteering flyers or gardening tools, I feel only a blank indifference, which makes me worry I'll never return to my previous level of independence. These thoughts of being useless and \"dead weight\" feel far too heavy to just go away.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your current emotional state is more likely a reaction to your recent life change and knee procedure, or could it be a sign of a more chronic condition that might recur in the future?\n\nPatient: I really feel this is a direct reaction to my knee procedure and the sudden loss of my active lifestyle. Before the fall, I was highly energetic, independent, and deeply involved in my community, and I have never experienced anything like this before. These feelings of uselessness only started once I realized I couldn't bounce back and participate in my usual activities.\n\nDoctor: Given that you've had these feelings for about a month and they seem closely tied to your knee procedure, do you think these feelings would likely recur if you faced another significant life change or health issue in the future, or do you believe this is a one-time response to your current situation?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure if this is something that would happen again with another change in the future. Right now, I'm just so overwhelmed by how I'm feeling in the present moment that it's hard to focus on anything else.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if your knee procedure had happened a year ago and you had fully recovered, you would have experienced this same level of persistent sadness, worthlessness, and loss of interest in activities, or do you believe this episode is specifically tied to the recent timing and circumstances of your life change?\n\nPatient: I believe these feelings are directly tied to the recent timing and the sudden loss of my active lifestyle. If the surgery had happened a year ago and I had fully recovered, I would likely be back to hiking, volunteering, and leading my workshops, so I wouldn't feel this way at all. It is really the sudden shift from being highly active to feeling like \"dead weight\" and worrying I won't recover my independence that has triggered this dark period.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that even if your knee fully heals and you regain your independence, the feelings of sadness, worthlessness, and loss of interest could still persist or recur in the future, or do you believe they would completely resolve once you're physically back to normal?\n\nPatient: Right now, it's so hard to even imagine my knee fully healing because of how stuck and hopeless I feel. I honestly don't know if these feelings would just go away, because this sadness and feeling of being useless feel so heavy and deeply rooted now. I really have no idea if I would ever just snap back to my old self.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your current emotional state would be better described as a single episode of depression that started after your knee procedure, or could it be the beginning of a pattern of depressive episodes that might recur in the future?\n\nPatient: I have never experienced anything like this before my knee injury, so it really feels like it is completely tied to this specific event. Because of that, I honestly don't know if this could become a recurring pattern in the future, or if it's just a one-time thing. I'm just not sure.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if you received treatment for your current depressive episode and it resolved, you would be at risk of having another episode in the future, or do you believe this is an isolated incident tied to your knee procedure?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure about future risks, and I haven't thought that far ahead. My mind is completely consumed right now with my physical limitations and feeling like a burden since my knee procedure, so it's hard to imagine anything beyond today.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that once you've recovered from this episode, you might be at risk of experiencing another episode of depression in the future, or do you believe this is a one-time occurrence directly related to your knee procedure and subsequent life changes?"

I have to remind myself to eat because nothing appeals to me, and by mid-afternoon, I've usually only picked at a piece of toast or some yogurt. It's just a heavy, weary feeling that comes over me when I'm exhausted.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling indifferent to activities you used to enjoy, but can you think of anything, no matter how small, that you still find some pleasure in or look forward to, even if it's just slightly?\n\nPatient: Honestly, there really isn't anything right now that brings me pleasure or that I look forward to.
